name: Vestige Pulse
description:
Vestige Pulse originated in the sub-basement rehearsal vaults of GLMZ's Tier 4 districts around 2197, born from a practice among heavily augmented musicians who discovered that partially degraded neural-memory implants produced rhythmic artifacts during playback — fragmented loops of half-remembered physical sensation, muscle memory, and proprioceptive echo. Performers deliberately induce controlled implant degradation to generate these unstable bio-temporal rhythms, layering them over stripped-down percussion frameworks. The result is music that pulses with an uncanny biological intimacy, as if the body itself is remembering how to move.

Listeners with BCI-compatible rigs experience Vestige Pulse not only as sound but as ghost-limb sensation — phantom gestures of dancing, labor, or intimacy that never quite resolve. The genre has attracted fierce loyalty from amputees, heavily augmented workers whose organic tissue percentage has dropped below 40%, and grief communities who use its dissociative warmth as a memorial medium. Bootleg vestige-captures of deceased individuals' neural residue have become a controversial subgenre, raising significant legal and ethical challenges around post-mortem data harvesting.
creator: various
tier_availability: Tiers 3–5; licensed BCI-lounge circuits in Tier 2; banned from Tier 1 residential zones
legality: Legal with certified implant-degradation waivers; post-mortem residue subgenre operates in legal grey zone
audience: Heavily augmented workers, amputee communities, grief collectives, BCI hobbyists, underground memorial culture
cultural_impact: Vestige Pulse reshaped how GLMZ's lower tiers conceptualize memory, embodiment, and mourning. It forced corporate implant manufacturers to lobby for degradation-prevention mandates — arguing the practice accelerated hardware obsolescence — while civil liberties groups countered that citizens have the right to experience and repurpose their own decaying data. The genre inadvertently created a new vocabulary around 'neural inheritance,' influencing inheritance law debates regarding whether a person's implant-stored sensation-memories constitute transferable property. Its emotional rawness has been credited with reducing social isolation metrics in Tier 4 by a measurable margin, though the methodology behind that statistic remains disputed.
story_hooks: A grief counselor discovers her deceased partner's vestige-capture is circulating as an unauthorized club track
An implant technician deliberately undersells degradation repair to supply raw material to vestige producers
A Tier 2 corporate heir becomes addicted to bootleg Tier 4 vestige-captures of manual laborers, seeking sensation their sanitized life cannot provide
